synthesis.paragraph: Four of today's papers carry the tag "Urban Transport and Accessibility", focusing on spatial exclusion on Vancouver's public golf courses, a visual choice experiment on urban street redesigns in Switzerland, a computer-assisted web-based personal interview method for capturing mobility in Bangladesh, and extreme rail-transit commutes in Shanghai. Outside of this group, one paper analyzed panel data from 287 Chinese cities to evaluate how artificial intelligence industrial agglomeration affects regional innovation. Another study analyzed urban shrinkage in medium-sized cities across Germany and Poland over a 15-year period. Finally, a third paper analyzed consumer reactions to the transition from reward-only to sanction-based algorithmic driver monitoring in insurance products.
